q: The Mandelbrot set M is computable in the sense that there exists an algorithm to compute membership to arbitrary precision. More precisely:
opts: The boundary ∂M is not computably enumerable
M is computable in the sense of computable analysis (its characteristic function is computable on the complement of ∂M)
exp: The Mandelbrot set M is computably closed: given c, one can compute arbitrarily tight approximations to the distance from c to M. The interior can be confirmed computably (hyperbolic components are computable). The computability of ∂M is subtle—local connectedness (MLC) would help but is unproven.
